answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making each registration post a time-locked surety. A new agent must stake the kernel-grade minimum collateral and hold it for one full epoch before its weight counts. Every clone owes that same lock separately, so flooding costs the attacker linearly in capital. Stakes are slashed when a clone is caught farming rewards, pushing expected profit negative. Re-using stake for extra seats needs distinct human-attested walnut credentials, which throttle capital recycling. Weight then grows along a slow trellis of trust, so late clones stay powerless.
